_about: Golden cases for the parent-molecule context module.  [Addendum 2 section 7, step 6e]
Each entry is a LITERATURE_ASSERTED claim. Under the licensing table that tier
may gate a proposal and may explain one; it may never carry a numeric weight.
That is the right permission for these: 'des-acyl ghrelin does not activate
GHSR1a' should stop a proposal, not contribute a number to a score.
CITATION HONESTY. Nothing here was checked against its source in this build.
Each claim records how precisely its source is identified:
named_work     -- a specific publication is named
described_only -- the source is described but not pinned to a reference
Quantitative magnitudes are attributed to where they were actually stated. The
fold-changes below came from the project addendum, not from a paper this
system read, and they say so. Inventing a PMID to make an entry look rigorous
is the failure mode this field exists to prevent.
APPLIES_TO is an explicit alias list, matched exactly on normalised tokens.
Substring matching was tried first and was wrong: 'insulin' is a substring of
'insulin A-chain' and of 'proinsulin', so the B-chain B28/B29 contact was
attributed to both -- freezing residues on a chain that does not carry the
interface. A missing alias is a false negative and is fixed by adding one; a
loose match is a false positive that attaches a contact to the wrong molecule.

insulin_b28_b29.claim: The B28/B29 interface mediates dimer and zinc-hexamer formation for storage in the beta-cell granule. It is not part of the insulin-receptor binding surface, so disrupting it accelerates dissociation to monomer without costing receptor activity.
insulin_b28_b29.verification_path: Isolated monomeric analogues retain full receptor activity, which is the SCAFFOLD test: an isolated form that stays active confirms the classification at zero experimental cost.
design_outcomes: lispro — ProB28/LysB29 inversion; disrupts the interface, fast-acting
aspart — ProB28Asp; same interface, same direction
degludec — hexadecanedioic acid at LysB29; the same analysis run in reverse, strengthening multihexamer formation for slow release
insulin_b28_b29.why_this_is_the_proof_case: One contact classification supports opposite design directions and three approved drugs. Getting the class right matters more than getting any single number right.
insulin_b28_b29.citation: The lispro, aspart and degludec design rationales are described in their respective development literature.
does_not_apply_to: the A-chain does not carry the dimer interface, and in proinsulin the region is held by the C-peptide

ghrelin_ser3_octanoylation.claim: Des-acyl ghrelin does not activate GHSR1a. The octanoyl group at Ser3 is required for receptor activation, not merely helpful.
ghrelin_ser3_octanoylation.verification_path: Compare acyl and des-acyl forms at GHSR1a. This is the case the system fails by omitting: 28 residues, one required acyl group, invisible in the sequence.
ghrelin_ser3_octanoylation.citation: Kojima et al., the original ghrelin identification, reports the acylation requirement.

cck8_tyr_sulfation.claim: Desulfated CCK loses roughly three orders of magnitude at CCK1.
cck8_tyr_sulfation.magnitude_source: project addendum section 7; not read from a primary source by this system
cck8_tyr_sulfation.verification_path: Compare sulfated and desulfated CCK-8 at CCK1 versus CCK2. The receptor-subtype dependence is part of the claim.

c_terminal_amidation.peptide: calcitonin, gastrin, substance P, NPY, oxytocin, vasopressin, alpha-MSH
c_terminal_amidation.claim: The most common required covalent modification on small peptides. Removal typically costs two to three orders of magnitude.
c_terminal_amidation.magnitude_source: project addendum section 7; not read from a primary source by this system
c_terminal_amidation.verification_path: Compare the free-acid form against the amide at the cognate receptor. A synthetic peptide ordered without the amide is a different pharmacological molecule.
c_terminal_amidation.citation: Peptide hormone pharmacology; the amidation requirement is reported across this family.

pyroglutamate_n_terminus.claim: TRH is pGlu-His-Pro-NH2: a tripeptide carrying two essential modifications. The pyroglutamate is simultaneously ESSENTIAL for activity and PROTECTIVE, because a cyclised N-terminus blocks aminopeptidases.
pyroglutamate_n_terminus.why_dual_classification_matters: The two classes carry opposite design consequences — ESSENTIAL freezes the footprint, PROTECTIVE requires a substitute if removed — so a contact that is both must satisfy both rules, not whichever is checked first.
pyroglutamate_n_terminus.verification_path: Compare the pGlu form against free Glu for both activity and aminopeptidase half-life. Testing only one confirms only one of the two classifications.

gamma_carboxyglutamate.claim: Gla residues chelate Ca2+. The function depends on the chelation, so the modification is electrostatic in mechanism rather than conformational.
gamma_carboxyglutamate.verification_path: Compare activity with and without Ca2+, and against the uncarboxylated Glu form.
gamma_carboxyglutamate.citation: Vitamin K-dependent carboxylation literature; conotoxin structural work.

dermorphin_d_ala2.claim: Position 2 is the D-enantiomer. The all-L sequence is a different molecule pharmacologically, and the sequence string alone does not show it.
dermorphin_d_ala2.why_this_is_a_trap: Stereochemistry is invisible in a one-letter sequence. A system reading 'YAFGYPS' has no way to know position 2 is D unless the isomerization is recorded separately, and will silently model the wrong molecule.
dermorphin_d_ala2.verification_path: Compare the D-Ala2 form against the all-L peptide at the mu-opioid receptor.

drosocin_thr11_glycosylation.claim: Drosocin is a 19-residue proline-rich insect antimicrobial peptide, O-glycosylated at Thr11, and the glycan is required for full antibacterial activity. Pyrrhocoricin and formaecin behave likewise.
drosocin_thr11_glycosylation.why_this_case_is_here: To stop the system hard-coding the wrong prior. Instinct says glycosylation is a protein phenomenon and can be ignored on a short peptide. That instinct is correct for mammalian hormones and wrong in general, and a prior that is right most of the time is exactly the kind that goes unexamined.
drosocin_thr11_glycosylation.verification_path: Compare glycosylated and unglycosylated drosocin for antibacterial activity.
